title: variance-propagation-sidecar-probe-notes-2026-06-21
content:
Meeting: Performance & Benchmarking sync — sidecar probe / variance propagation capture
Date: 2026-06-21 10:30-11:15 PT
Location: eng-serving-runtime weekly / Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (owner), Rafael Ortega, Chen Li, Sofia Alvarez, Ethan Brooks, notes by Maya
Objective: Capture a reproducible profile for the recent p95 drift we saw in Dedicated pools when the sidecar (request-multiplexer) is enabled; agree on short experiments and rollforward plan to reduce tail variance before the Friday release window.

1) TL;DR summary
- Observed: p95 increased ~18–25% across mixed-seq runs during sidecar routing tests staged on dedicated-qa. Baseline without sidecar: p95 ~42ms; with sidecar enabled: p95 ~52ms on same hardware and model combo. p50 remained stable.
- Hypothesis: variance is propagated by the sidecar's per-request routing jitter + occasional thread-pool transient stalls when a small fraction of requests hit cache-repopulate paths.
- Repro steps validated in probe harness (see linked gs:// run traces). We have a minimal repro that reliably shows the p95 jump on runs with sequence length distribution skewed to tail tokens > 380.
- Next actions: (A) Run experiment matrix to confirm whether batching window jitter or CPU contention is dominant (owner: Rafael). (B) Add a short-circuit path in the sidecar for hot prefix KV-cache hits (owner: Chen). (C) Increase sidecar worker threads in Dedicated-qa to test throughput/latency tradeoff (owner: Sofia). (D) Prepare rollback plan and metric alert tweaks for Friday release (owner: Ethan).

2) Observed signals and artifacts
- Metrics snapshot (mixed-seq, model=rwd-medium-1280, 8xA10s equivalent):
  - baseline (no-sidecar): p50=12ms, p95=42ms, p99=118ms, qps=1200
  - sidecar-default: p50=13ms, p95=52ms, p99=140ms, qps=1185
  - sidecar-with-cache-warm: p50=12ms, p95=47ms, p99=122ms, qps=1198
- Traces: sampled traces show 1. per-request enqueue latency in sidecar varying 0.3–4.7ms and 2. occasional 10–30ms spikes in downstream kernel scheduling when KV-cache refill happens.
- Logs: sidecar logs show ~0.6% of requests enter the cache-miss cold path; those correlate with the highest p99 samples.
- Environment note: This regressed only when the sidecar was placed in front of the multiplexer (new routing code merged last week, PR linked). No regression when sidecar is bypassed.

3) Repro steps used in probe harness (for engineers to reproduce locally)
- Start dedicated-qa cluster tag=dedicated-qa-2026-06-18, model=rwd-medium-1280, 8 shards.
- Launch probe: scripts/bench/sidecar_probe.sh --workload mixed-seq --seq-dist heavy-tail --qps 1200 --duration 15m --capture-traces gs://redwood-bench/sidecar-probe/2026-06-21/runs/run-01
- Toggle sidecar: bench toggle-sidecar --enable/--disable in the same run to capture paired traces.
- Ensure KV-cache is cold between paired runs (stop/restart runtime or flush prefix-cache via admin API).
- Collect traces with perf+strace capture and upload to bucket.

4) Hypotheses (ranked)
- H1 (highest): Sidecar adds small request scheduling jitter; when combined with rare KV-cache refills that block kernel scheduling (for ~10–30ms) this pushes a fraction of requests into the p95 bucket.
- H2: Batching window alignment between sidecar and runtime causes microbursts where the runtime sees short bursts of requests and threads contend for IO locks.
- H3: Network egress jitter at the host NIC when flows burst from multiple sidecars (less likely; infra saw no link-level drops).

5) Experiment matrix (short runs, owners, acceptance criteria)
- E1: Isolate sidecar scheduling: increase sidecar worker threads from default 4 -> 8 and measure p95 change (owner: Sofia). Acceptance: p95 reduces by >=6% without p50 regression and CPU steady-state < 85%.
- E2: Short-circuit hot prefix: add a bypass codepath for prefix-KV cache hits in sidecar returns path (owner: Chen). Acceptance: p95 reduces and p99 tail drops; rollout to canary if good.
- E3: Batching smoothing: add 1–2ms randomized jitter to sidecar batching window to de-correlate bursts (owner: Rafael). Acceptance: reduced p95 variance across runs; no cost increase >2% tokens/sec.
- E4: Kernel scheduling probe: force synthetic cache misses to reproduce 10–30ms scheduling stalls under controlled CPU isolation (owner: Rafael + SRE). Acceptance: reproduce the spike locally to prove causal path.

6) Short experiment results (quick runs done during meeting)
- E1 quick: threads=8 run (10m) -> p95=49ms (down from 52), p99 still ~135ms. CPU increased from 62% -> 77% on sidecar host. Good signal but partial improvement.
- E3 quick: batching-window +1ms jitter -> p95=50ms, variance across runs reduced (stdev p95 from 3.8ms -> 2.1ms).
- E2 quick: prototype bypass (dev flag) -> p95=46ms, p99=125ms. This looks promising but prototype path needs safety checks.

7) Action items (owners + ETA)
- Rafael: run full matrix (E1,E3,E4) with 30m runs across 3 seeds, upload traces and perf profiles. ETA: 2026-06-23 EOD.
- Chen: harden prefix bypass path, add metrics and safety checks (fall back on cache false positives), open PR for review. ETA: 2026-06-24. PR: github link in linked_artifacts.
- Sofia: test sidecar worker thread tuning across instance types (A10 vs T4 cost tradeoffs) and provide config recommendation. ETA: 2026-06-24.
- Ethan: prepare rollback plan + alert tuning for Friday release: add temporary alert to treat p95 spikes as WARN not P1, and ensure canary disables sidecar if sustained p95 > 20% over baseline for 5m. ETA: 2026-06-23.
- Maya (owner): coordinate canary window for Friday release + ensure exec summary for weekly eng sync. ETA: 2026-06-25 morning.

8) Risks & mitigation
- Risk: If bypass path has correctness edge cases (prefix false hits) we may introduce quality regressions. Mitigation: include conservative safety checks and disable bypass in presence of ambiguous key signatures.
- Risk: Increasing sidecar workers increases CPU footprint and cost. Mitigation: limit to canary and measure tokens/sec, scale by pool size.

9) Notes to reviewers / questions unresolved
- Need SRE input on whether kernel scheduling stalls show up in host-level perf counters we can alert on (can we add perf counters to the observability dashboard?). (tag: @sre)
- Decide if bypass becomes default for Dedicated only or for Hosted as well; Hosted runs may not need bypass because they have larger multi-tenant pooling and observed no regression.
- Confirm if billing/cost impact of thread increases should be handled via dedicated-qa only or folded into forecast for Dedicated customers. (tag: finance question)

10) Follow-ups / next meeting
- Quick sync Tue 2026-06-23 09:00 PT to review Rafael's full-matrix results and Chen's PR review notes.
- If E2 passes safety checks, plan canary rollout on Fri 2026-06-25 02:00 PT during low-traffic window.

Appendix: quick links and commands
- Repro script: scripts/bench/sidecar_probe.sh
- Trace bucket: gs://redwood-bench/sidecar-probe/2026-06-21/runs/
- Dev flag to enable bypass: admin-api /sidecar/flags?bypass_hot_prefix=1
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123

Raw notes: (copied from live chat during meeting)
- "I can reproduce locally when I hammer the heavy-tail sequence distribution, p50 okay but p95 jumps" — Rafael
- "Prototype bypass showed promising drop in p95 but need to ensure we don't return stale prefixes" — Chen
- "If we do thread bump, document cost tradeoffs; put a guard so it only happens during canary" — Sofia
- "I'll add temporary alert and rollback playbook tonight so release isn't blocked" — Ethan

End of notes.
